proposals.before: His father Fan, courtesy name Feique, was posthumously made Grand Preceptor by Wei and given posthumous name Duke Xiaoxuan.
proposals.after: His father Fan, courtesy name Feique, was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant by Wei and given the posthumous title Duke Xiaoxuan.

proposals.before: His mother Lady Shan was enfeoffed Lady of the Commandery; a daughter was made Lady Attendant Within and entered to serve the empress.
proposals.after: His mother Lady Shan was enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery, appointed Female Palace Attendant, and entered to serve the empress.
proposals.reason: The subject remains Lady Shan throughout; 女侍中 is her palace office and does not introduce an otherwise unmentioned daughter.

proposals.before: Erzhu Rong still held Bing Province; Gao Huan meant to attack him and left Yue to guard the capital, promoting him to grand general of the flying cavalry and honorary equal to the three ducal ministers.

proposals.reason: 尒朱兆 is Erzhu Zhao; Erzhu Rong is a different person (尔朱荣).

proposals.before: At that time Erzhu Rong still held Bing Province; the High Ancestor was about to attack him and ordered Yue to remain guarding the capital, promoting him to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry and Honorary Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
proposals.after: At that time Erzhu Zhao still held Bing Province; the High Ancestor was about to attack him and ordered Yue to remain guarding the capital, promoting him to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry and Honorary Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
proposals.reason: 尒朱兆 names Erzhu Zhao, not Erzhu Rong; the literal field repeats the same wrong-person substitution.

proposals.after: In the sixth year, for merit, he was made palace attendant and grand commandant; other offices unchanged; separately enfeoffed viscount of Xinchang.

proposals.before: In the sixth year, for merit he was made Palace Attendant and Grand Preceptor; the rest as before; separately enfeoffed Viscount of Xinchang.

proposals.after: When Houzhu was defeated at Jin Province, the Empress Dowager returned to the capital by the Tumen Road; an edict put Mai in overall command of troops to escort her.

proposals.after: When Houzhu was defeated at Jin Province, the Empress Dowager returned to the capital by the Tumen Road; an edict ordered Mai to take overall command of troops and escort the Empress Dowager.

proposals.before: Appraisal: Zhao Commandery — heroic and grand; bearing composed, mien upright.
proposals.after: Appraisal: The Prince of Zhao Commandery was heroic and imposing, his bearing composed and upright.
proposals.reason: 趙郡 abbreviates the Prince of Zhao Commandery, while 風範凝正 describes his composed and upright bearing; the current English reads as a place-name fragment.

proposals.before: Appraisal: Zhao Commandery — heroic and grand; bearing and mien composed and upright.
proposals.after: Appraisal: The Prince of Zhao Commandery was heroic and imposing; his bearing and mien were composed and upright.
proposals.reason: 趙郡 abbreviates the prince rather than naming a place here, and the fragmentary predicates need an expressed English subject and verb.

proposals.before: Illustrious Qinghe — by him the state was governed.
proposals.after: Illustrious was the Prince of Qinghe, through whom the state was governed.
proposals.reason: 清河 abbreviates the Prince of Qinghe, and the revised sentence restores the personal referent and natural English syntax without changing 于以經國.

proposals.before: Illustrious Qinghe — by him the state was ordered.
proposals.after: Illustrious was the Prince of Qinghe; through him the state was ordered.
proposals.reason: 清河 abbreviates the Prince of Qinghe, so the literal English should identify the person and form a grammatical sentence.

proposals.before: A small flaw at the end of the road — not a collapse of virtue.
proposals.after: A minor failing at the end did not ruin his virtue.
proposals.reason: 末路 means the final stage of his life or career here, not a literal road; the revision preserves the contrast with 非為敗德 in natural English.

proposals.before: A small stain at the final road — not a ruin of virtue.
proposals.after: A small flaw at the end did not amount to ruined virtue.
proposals.reason: 末路 is the end of Gao Yue's course or career, not a literal road; the literal field should preserve the contrast without unidiomatic calques.

decisions.after: His mother, Lady Shan, was enfeoffed as Lady of the Commandery, appointed Female Palace Attendant, and entered the palace to serve the empress.
decisions.reason: Lady Shan remains the grammatical subject: 女侍中 is the office to which she was appointed, not a daughter introduced by 女.

decisions.reason: The source lists Lady Shan's enfeoffment, appointment as 女侍中, and palace service in one subject chain; the literal repair removes the invented daughter.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 母山氏，封為郡君，授女侍中，入侍皇后。

decisions.reason: 尒朱兆 is Erzhu Zhao. Erzhu Rong is a different person whose name ends in 榮, so the old English points to the wrong historical figure.

decisions.reason: The literal field repeats the same wrong-person substitution; 尒朱兆 unequivocally names Erzhu Zhao.

decisions.after: In the sixth year, he was rewarded for his merit with appointment as palace attendant and grand commandant; his other offices remained unchanged, and he was separately enfeoffed as Viscount of Xinchang.
decisions.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, and 別封新昌縣子 separately enfeoffs Gao Yue as Viscount of Xinchang; the reviewed prose preserves both facts.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 六年，以功除侍中、太尉，餘如故，別封新昌縣子。

decisions.reason: The literal field must also distinguish 太尉 from 太師. Grand Commandant is the correct office in this appointment sequence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 六年，以功除侍中、太尉，餘如故，別封新昌縣子。

decisions.after: When Gao Zhan died, several days after the burial, Rui, together with Prince of Fengyi Gao Run, Prince of Ande Gao Yanzong, and Yuan Wenyao, memorialized the Last Emperor, saying, "He Shikai should not continue to hold an inner appointment."
decisions.reason: 馮翊 is Fengyi, not Fenyang. The reviewed sentence also restores the comma needed to separate the burial phrase from Rui as subject.
